mainTopic: The איסור of offering a קרבן while owning חמץ (sources and contradictions), and the משנה's description of how the קרבן פסח was slaughtered in three groups.
overview: The amud opens by settling two contradictions between ברייתות about offering a קרבן while owning חמץ. Both ברייתות follow רבי שמעון. The מליקה difference is about timing: the fourteenth of ניסן versus חול המועד. The הקטרה difference is a dispute among תנאים over whether burning is compared to slaughtering. The גמרא then explains the sources in the משנה: רבי יהודה reads זבחי as the תמיד, and רבי שמעון reads the doubled זבחי as "זבח" and "זבחיי" to split the fourteenth from the festival. Next it challenges רבי שמעון's ruling about a פסח slaughtered during the festival, since that ruling seems to imply that a פסח needs עקירה to become a שלמים. רבי חייא בר גמדא answers that the case is owners who were deferred to פסח שני. A new משנה then describes the slaughter of the פסח in three groups: the trumpet blasts, the rows of כהנים passing the blood, the saying of הלל, what changes on שבת, and how the animals were hung and skinned. It ends as רבי אליעזר begins a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two contradictions between the ברייתות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two ברייתות contradict each other on מליקה and on הקטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a contradiction between pinching and pinching, and a contradiction between burning and burning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lines up the two ברייתות it just quoted and shows that they disagree on two points: מליקה and הקטרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא includes the one who burns (מקטיר) in the איסור of offering with חמץ around, but it does not include the one who pinches (מולק). The second ברייתא includes the one who pinches but does not mention burning. If both ברייתות describe the same איסור, they cannot both be right.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: a contradiction or challenge
Pinching the neck of a bird offering with the כהן's fingernail
Burning the sacrificial parts on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: The pattern "X אַ-X" (מליקה אמליקה) means 'X in this source against X in that source.' It does not mean two different actions.

phrases.english: There is a contradiction: pinching against pinching,
phrases.notes: The first ברייתא excludes the one who pinches, and the second includes him.

phrases.english: there is a contradiction: burning against burning!
phrases.notes: The first ברייתא includes the one who burns, and the second leaves him out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two ברייתות cited on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about who is included in the איסור of offering with חמץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each ברייתא includes an action that the other one leaves out, so they cannot both be describing the same rule.

steps.title: The second ברייתא contradicts itself if read as one case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the question around. By the questioner's own logic, the second ברייתא is self-contradictory, so the assumption behind the question must be wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, you should ask about this ברייתא itself! It teaches 'They only said this about the פסח,' and then it teaches 'whether one slaughters, sprinkles, pinches, or sprinkles bird blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a counter-question. It shows that the second ברייתא cannot be read as a single uniform case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא says the איסור applies 'only to the פסח.' Yet it then lists מליקה and הזאה, which are done only to bird offerings, and a פסח is never a bird. So the ברייתא must be speaking about two different time frames. This sets up the real answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: a counter-challenge that uses the questioner's own assumption against him
It itself: the same source contradicts itself
And then it goes on to teach
The one who sprinkles the blood (here, of a bird offering)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the contradiction yet. It only proves that the second ברייתא has two parts that refer to different situations. The real answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, ask about the ברייתא itself.

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּפֶסַח בִּלְבַד,
phrases.english: For it teaches: They said this only about the Paschal lamb,
and then it teaches:
whether one slaughters or one sprinkles the blood,
or one pinches, or one sprinkles bird blood!
phrases.notes: Pinching and sprinkling bird blood apply only to birds, never to a פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the hidden assumption of step 1, that each ברייתא describes one uniform situation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The premise that the second ברייתא speaks about a single case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Only the פסח' cannot include bird actions, so the ברייתא must cover more than one time or case.

steps.title: מליקה: the fourteenth of ניסן versus חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: Both ברייתות follow רבי שמעון. The ruling that excludes מליקה is about the fourteenth of ניסן, and the ruling that includes it is about חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this and that follow רבי שמעון. Pinching versus pinching is no difficulty: here it means the fourteenth, there it means חול המועד. Both are רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the מליקה contradiction by assigning each ruling to a different day, using רבי שמעון's view from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון holds that on the fourteenth only the פסח is included, and other offerings are פטור. During חול המועד, other offerings (including birds) are חייב. So the ruling that leaves out the מולק refers to the fourteenth, and the ruling that includes him refers to חול המועד.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one: both sources
Here... there: assigning each source to a different case
The fourteenth of ניסן, when the פסח is offered
The intermediate days of the festival
Both this and that

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי שמעון's split between the fourteenth and חול המועד explains differences between ברייתות that look like they contradict.

phrases.english: Rather: both this and that follow Rabbi Shimon.
Pinching against pinching is no difficulty:
here, it refers to the fourteenth of Nisan,
phrases.notes: Excluded, because on the fourteenth only the פסח is included.

phrases.english: there, it refers to the intermediate days of the festival.
phrases.notes: Included, because other offerings are חייב then.

phrases.english: And both are the opinion of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 2's insight that the ברייתא covers different times, and uses it to answer the מליקה contradiction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: כאן וכאן: different time frames, same תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות describe the same day, so they contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Under רבי שמעון, the fourteenth excludes bird offerings and חול המועד includes them.

steps.title: הקטרה: a dispute among תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The הקטרה contradiction reflects a dispute among תנאים over whether burning is compared to slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Burning versus burning is also no difficulty; it is a dispute of תנאים. Some compare burning to slaughtering, and some do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the second contradiction by saying the two ברייתות reflect two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that includes the מקטיר follows a תנא who uses a היקש to compare burning to שחיטה. The one that leaves burning out follows a תנא who does not make that comparison. Unlike מליקה, this is a real disagreement, not a difference of time.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among תנאים
Compares by היקש: derives one law from another through a textual link
Ritual slaughter

steps.whatToRemember: The מליקה contradiction is solved by time: the fourteenth versus חול המועד. The הקטרה contradiction is solved by a real dispute among תנאים: whether burning is compared to slaughtering.

phrases.english: Burning against burning is also no difficulty:
it is a dispute of tanna'im.
For there is one who compares burning to slaughtering,
phrases.notes: This matches רב פפא's approach earlier.

phrases.english: and there is one who does not compare them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַקְטָרָה אַהַקְטָרָה נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא — תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of the question from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: תנאי היא: the sources reflect different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות share one view on הקטרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whether הקטרה is included depends on whether one compares it to שחיטה.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי יהודה's view about the תמיד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's line from the משנה and asks what his reasoning is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהודה says, even the daily offering, etc. What is רבי יהודה's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה. It quotes רבי יהודה, who says you are also liable for slaughtering the תמיד while owning חמץ, and asks for his source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic prohibition in the משנה is about the קרבן פסח. רבי יהודה adds the afternoon תמיד of ערב פסח. The גמרא wants to know what in the פסוק makes him include it.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily communal burnt-offering, brought every morning and afternoon
What is the reason? (asks for the source or logic behind a view)
Etc. The rest of the quote is in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Even the daily offering, etc.
phrases.notes: He means one is liable for slaughtering the afternoon תמיד on ערב פסח while owning חמץ.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the contradiction between the ברייתות to explain the משנה's individual views.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק or reading teaches that the תמיד is included in the prohibition.

steps.title: "My sacrifice" means the offering set aside for ה׳: the תמיד
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads זבחי as "the sacrifice that is especially Mine," which is the תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: "My sacrifice" means the sacrifice that is designated for Me. And which one is that? The תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word זבחי ("My sacrifice") in the פסוק points to the תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "My" suggests a קרבן that belongs especially to ה׳. The תמיד is the most constant, regular offering of the בית המקדש, so רבי יהודה sees it as "His" sacrifice. That is why it is included alongside the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: "My sacrifice", the word in the פסוק about not offering with חמץ
Designated or set aside especially for Me
"He would say to you": the גמרא speaking on behalf of the תנא

phrases.english: He would say to you:
"My sacrifice" means a sacrifice that is designated to Me,
phrases.notes: From the פסוק "You shall not offer the blood of My sacrifice with חמץ".

phrases.english: And what is it? The daily offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word זבחי ("My sacrifice") refers to the קרבן most especially belonging to ה׳, the תמיד.

steps.title: What is the source for רבי שמעון's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's position from the משנה and asks for his reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי שמעון says, the פסח on the fourteenth, etc. What is רבי שמעון's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next opinion in the משנה, רבי שמעון's, and asks for his source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון splits the rule by time. On the fourteenth of ניסן, only the פסח carries liability. During the festival itself, every sacrifice does. The גמרא wants to know where the פסוק teaches this split.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourteenth of ניסן, ערב פסח, when the קרבן פסח is slaughtered

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
The Paschal lamb on the fourteenth, etc.
phrases.notes: On the fourteenth, only the פסח brings liability. During the festival, all sacrifices do.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same "what is his reason" pattern as step 5, now for the next תנא in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that shows the split between the fourteenth (only the פסח) and the festival (all sacrifices).

steps.title: זבחי is written twice, so read it as "זבח" and "זבחיי"
steps.stepSummary: The word זבחי appears in two פסוקים. Combined, they are read as "a sacrifice" (singular) and "My sacrifices" (plural).
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is written "My sacrifice," "My sacrifice" two times. Read into it: "a sacrifice" and "My sacrifices."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the Torah repeats the word זבחי in two places. רבי שמעון reads the two together as one sacrifice plus all of ה׳'s sacrifices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two appearances (שמות כג:יח and לד:כה) are combined and the letters are reread as two words. "זבח" means one particular sacrifice, the פסח. "זבחיי" means all My sacrifices. So the law covers both the פסח and other קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Two times
Read into it: a rereading of the letters to draw out a teaching
"My sacrifices" (plural)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a change to the written Torah. It is a דרשה that rereads the combined letters of the two appearances of זבחי to draw out two meanings.

phrases.english: As it is written "My sacrifice," "My sacrifice," two times,
phrases.notes: The two places are שמות כג:יח and שמות לד:כה.

phrases.english: Read into it: "a sacrifice," "My sacrifices."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The repeated זבחי is read as "זבח" (the פסח) and "זבחיי" (all sacrifices). Both are included.

steps.title: Why did the Torah split the words instead of just writing "My sacrifices"?
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah wanted to include all sacrifices, why did it divide the word into two places instead of writing "זבחיי" once?
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law did the Torah separate them from each other, and not simply write "My sacrifices"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the reading in step 8. If all sacrifices are included, why did the Torah split it up? This sets up the timing rule in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Writing "זבחיי" once would already include every sacrifice. The Torah instead wrote זבחי twice in separate places, so the split itself must be teaching something. That something is the difference between the fourteenth and the festival.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (asks what practical teaching something carries)
Divided them, separated them
"The Merciful One", a name for ה׳ as the Author of the Torah

phrases.english: For what law
did the Merciful One divide them from each other
and not write "My sacrifices"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the reading in step 8 had to come from two separate words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra law is taught by the Torah dividing זבח and זבחיי.

steps.title: When the פסח is offered, only the פסח counts; when it is not, all sacrifices count
steps.stepSummary: The split teaches timing. On the fourteenth, the day of the פסח, there is no liability for other sacrifices. During the festival, there is liability for all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: To say: at a time when there is "the sacrifice" (the פסח), one is not liable for "My sacrifices." At a time when there is no "sacrifice," one is liable for "My sacrifices."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the Torah separated the words to make a time-based rule. When the פסח is being brought, only it counts. At other times during the festival, all sacrifices count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "זבח" stands for the פסח, and it pushes aside "זבחיי" on its own day, the fourteenth. On the days of the festival, there is no פסח, so the rule for all sacrifices applies. This is exactly רבי שמעון's split in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: At a time when there is
At a time when there is not
Is liable

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון: on the fourteenth of ניסן, only the פסח slaughtered with חמץ brings liability. During the festival, every sacrifice does. The source is the two appearances of זבחי, read as "זבח" and "זבחיי."

phrases.english: To say:
At the time when there is "the sacrifice"
phrases.notes: The fourteenth, when the פסח is offered.

phrases.english: one is not liable for "My sacrifices."
At a time when there is no "sacrifice"
one is liable for "My sacrifices."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The split teaches that the presence of the פסח on the fourteenth excludes other sacrifices, while during the festival all sacrifices are included.

steps.title: Reading closely into the ruling about a פסח slaughtered during the festival
steps.stepSummary: From רבי שמעון's ruling, the גמרא infers that a פסח slaughtered during the festival with no stated intent is treated like one slaughtered for its own purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "During the festival, for its own purpose, he is exempt," etc. The reason he is liable is that he slaughtered it for a different purpose. But if he slaughtered it without stating any purpose, he would be exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's ruling about a פסח slaughtered during the festival and draws an inference from its exact wording. This sets up the next discussion in the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes him liable only when he slaughters "for a different purpose," because then it works as a valid שלמים. So if he slaughters with no stated intent, he must be exempt. That means such an animal still counts as a פסח, which is invalid on these days. In other words, outside its proper time a פסח keeps its identity unless it is actively switched to another purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: During the festival (חול המועד)
For its own purpose, slaughtered as a פסח
For a different purpose, slaughtered as a different קרבן
Without any stated intent
Exempt

steps.confusionAlert: The animal does not stop being a פסח. It stays a פסח, and that is exactly why it is invalid during the festival and why there is no liability. Only active intent for another purpose turns it into a valid שלמים, which brings liability.
steps.whyThisMatters: This inference shows how a פסח is treated during the rest of the year: does it need to be actively switched to another purpose to become valid? The גמרא's next discussion builds on this.

phrases.english: And during the festival, for its own purpose, he is exempt, etc.
phrases.notes: A quotation from the משנה (רבי שמעון).

phrases.english: The reason he is liable is that it was for a different purpose,
but without stated intent, he would be exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the source of רבי שמעון's view to a close reading of his ruling about the festival.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the משנה's wording: a פסח slaughtered during the festival with no stated intent is treated as a פסח, so it is invalid and brings no liability.

steps.title: Why should an unspecified פסח not count as a שלמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the inference from Step 11. During the rest of the year, a פסח is automatically treated as a שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why? A פסח during the rest of the year is a שלמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from Step 11, that a פסח slaughtered during the festival with no stated intent is treated as if it were slaughtered for its own purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון makes a person liable for slaughtering a פסח שלא לשמו during the festival while owning חמץ, because it then counts as a valid שלמים. Step 11 inferred that an unspecified slaughter is exempt. But a פסח outside its proper time is automatically a שלמים, so even an unspecified slaughter should count as a שלמים and make him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? (expresses surprise at a ruling)
the rest of the days of the year, meaning any time other than the 14th of ניסן
peace-offering; a leftover פסח becomes this

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'the rest of the year' includes the festival days themselves. Any time after the 14th, a פסח is outside its proper time.

phrases.english: Why?
A Paschal lamb during the rest of the days of the year
is a peace-offering!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? פֶּסַח בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה שְׁלָמִים הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference made in Step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that an unspecified פסח during the festival counts as לשמו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסח outside its time automatically becomes a שלמים, so an unspecified slaughter should count as a שלמים and make him liable

steps.title: So a פסח during the year would need active uprooting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws a troubling conclusion: a פסח at other times does not become a שלמים unless its status is actively uprooted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: a פסח during the rest of the year needs uprooting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that if Step 11's inference is correct, a surprising rule follows. A פסח at other times would need its owner to actively declare it something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we assume that a leftover פסח becomes a שלמים automatically. This conclusion would mean the opposite: it stays a פסח until someone performs עקירה. Because this clashes with the accepted view, it sets up the need for an answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this
uprooting; actively declaring that the animal is not being offered as a פסח

phrases.english: Learn from this
that a Paschal lamb during the rest of the days of the year
requires uprooting!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the problematic result of the challenge in Step 12
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Tentatively, a פסח outside its time would need עקירה. This conclusion is troubling and calls for an answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference of Step 11 that an unspecified פסח slaughtered during the festival is exempt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an unspecified פסח during the festival does not count as a שלמים, then a פסח outside its time would need עקירה to become a שלמים. That clashes with the accepted rule that it becomes a שלמים automatically.

steps.title: The case is owners who were impure and pushed off to פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר גמדא reports a group conclusion: רבי שמעון is speaking of owners who were טמאי מת and were deferred to פסח שני. Their animal still stands as a פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר גמדא said: It came out from the group, and they said: The case is where the owners were impure from a corpse and were pushed off to פסח שני. Without any stated intent, that animal stands to be a פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting רבי שמעון's ruling to one specific situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These owners still plan to bring this very animal on פסח שני. So even during the festival, it stands to be a פסח and does not automatically become a שלמים. A normal leftover פסח really does become a שלמים automatically, so there is no general rule requiring עקירה.

keyTerms.meaning: it emerged from the group; a conclusion the group agreed on, whose author was forgotten
people impure from contact with a corpse
the second פסח on 14 אייר for those who could not bring the first
its unspecified default status

steps.whatToRemember: A פסח outside its time normally becomes a שלמים automatically. The exception is an animal set aside for owners who were deferred to פסח שני, which still stands as a פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer keeps the general rule that a leftover פסח needs no עקירה, and explains רבי שמעון through a special case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said:
It emerged from the group, and they said:
for example, where the owners were impure from a corpse,
and are deferred to the second Passover,
so that, unspecified, it stands as a Paschal lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר גַּמְדָּא נִזְרְקָה מִפִּי חֲבוּרָה וְאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Steps 12-13
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every פסח outside its time needs עקירה
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a פסח set aside for owners deferred to פסח שני still stands as a פסח; others become a שלמים automatically

steps.title: New משנה: the פסח is slaughtered in three groups
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the פסח was slaughtered in three groups, based on three words in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The פסח is slaughtered in three groups, as it says: 'And the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall slaughter it.' That is: assembly, congregation, and Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the people bringing the פסח were divided into three separate groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses three words for the nation: קהל, עדה, and ישראל. Each word is read as a separate group, so the slaughter took place in three rounds.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה
groups
assembly, congregation, Israel; three words read as three groups

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The Paschal lamb is slaughtered in three groups,
as it is stated: “And they shall slaughter it,
the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel”:
assembly, and congregation, and Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסח is slaughtered in three separate groups, learned from three words in the פסוק

steps.title: The first group enters and the trumpets sound
steps.stepSummary: The first group fills the עזרה, the doors are locked, and the trumpets sound תקיעה, תרועה, תקיעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first group entered. The עזרה became full. They locked the doors of the עזרה. They blew a תקיעה, a תרועה, and a תקיעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the order of events step by step, beginning with the first group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The group is defined by how many people fit: once the עזרה is full, the doors close and the rest wait for the next round. The trumpet blasts were the same ones blown with every offering.

keyTerms.meaning: the Temple courtyard
they sounded a long blast, a broken blast, and a long blast

phrases.english: The first group entered,
the courtyard became filled,
they locked the doors of the courtyard,
they sounded a long blast, a broken blast, and a long blast,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's description of the procedure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each group entered until the עזרה was full, the doors were locked, and the trumpets were sounded

steps.title: כהנים stand in rows with silver and gold bowls
steps.stepSummary: The כהנים stood in rows holding bowls to receive the blood. Each row was all silver or all gold, never mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהנים stand in many rows, holding silver bowls and gold bowls. One row was all silver, and one row was all gold. They were not mixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes how the כהנים were arranged to receive the blood and pass it toward the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rows of כהנים passed the bowls of blood from the place of slaughter to the מזבח. Keeping each row to one metal made the display orderly and beautiful.

keyTerms.meaning: rows
bowls used to receive the blood
mixed together

phrases.english: The priests stand in rows upon rows,
and in their hands are bowls of silver and bowls of gold.
A row that was entirely silver was all silver,
and a row that was entirely gold was all gold;
they were not mixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of the procedure
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים stood in rows, and each row held only silver bowls or only gold bowls

steps.title: The bowls had no flat bases
steps.stepSummary: The bowls were made without flat bases, so the כהנים could not put them down and let the blood congeal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bowls did not have flat bases, because the כהנים might put them down and the blood would congeal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a design detail about the bowls and explains the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Congealed blood cannot be sprinkled on the מזבח, so the offering would be ruined. A bowl that cannot stand forces the כהן to keep holding it and pass it on right away.

keyTerms.meaning: bases, flat bottoms
the blood will congeal

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's procedure: three groups, a full עזרה, locked doors, trumpet blasts, and rows of כהנים passing the blood in unmixed silver or gold bowls that had no bases, so the blood would not congeal.

phrases.english: And the bowls did not have bases,
lest they set them down and the blood congeal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail about the bowls from Step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bowls had no bases, so they could not be set down and the blood would not congeal

steps.title: The blood is passed down a line of כהנים to the altar
steps.stepSummary: A ישראל may slaughter. A כהן catches the blood, and the bowl is passed from כהן to כהן. Each one takes a full bowl and hands back an empty one. The כהן nearest the מזבח throws the blood once toward the יסוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A regular Jew slaughters and the כהן catches the blood. He hands it to the next כהן, who hands it to the next. Each one takes the full bowl and passes back the empty one. The כהן closest to the altar throws it once toward the altar's base.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the picture of the first group in the עזרה and explains how the blood travels from the animal to the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering does not need a כהן, so a ישראל can do it. Catching and carrying the blood is כהן work, so a whole chain of כהנים moves full bowls forward and empty bowls back, like a conveyor belt. Only one throw is needed, aimed at the side of the מזבח that has a יסוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering. A non-כהן is allowed to do it.
Catching the blood in a bowl. Only a כהן may do it.
Throwing the blood onto the altar
The base ledge at the bottom of the מזבח
Empty (the empty bowl being returned)

steps.confusionAlert: The full bowls go forward and the empty bowls come back down the same line at the same time. It is a two-way chain, not one כהן walking back and forth.

phrases.english: An Israelite slaughtered, and the priest received the blood.
He gives it to his fellow, and his fellow to his fellow.

phrases.aramaic: וּמְקַבֵּל אֶת הַמָּלֵא, וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרֵיקָן.
phrases.english: He receives the full bowl and returns the empty one.
The priest who is closest to the altar
throws it with one throw opposite the base.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the bowls of step 18 and shows how those bowls were used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל may slaughter. כהנים pass the blood in a chain, and the nearest כהן throws it once toward the יסוד.

steps.title: The second and third groups follow the same order
steps.stepSummary: The first group leaves and the second enters. Then the second leaves and the third enters. All three groups do everything the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first group went out and the second came in. The second went out and the third came in. Whatever the first group did, the second and third did the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves the scene forward from group one to groups two and three and tells us the procedure does not change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 described only the first group. This step tells us that everything said about it (locked doors, trumpets, rows of כהנים, one throw) repeats for each group, so the משנה does not need to say it again.

keyTerms.meaning: A group (here, one of the three groups bringing the פסח)
It went out
It came in

phrases.aramaic: יָצְתָה כַּת רִאשׁוֹנָה, וְנִכְנְסָה כַּת שְׁנִיָּה.
phrases.english: The first group went out, and the second group came in.
The second went out, and the third came in.
As was the procedure of the first,
so was the procedure of the second and the third.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָצְתָה כַּת רִאשׁוֹנָה, וְנִכְנְסָה כַּת שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the first group's procedure to the other two groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three groups follow the identical procedure.

steps.title: They said הלל while slaughtering, repeating if needed
steps.stepSummary: While the קרבנות were being slaughtered, the people said הלל. If they finished, they started again, and if needed a third time. In practice they never got to a third time.
steps.simpleTranslation: They read the הלל. If they finished, they said it again. If they finished the second time, they said it a third time. But it never actually reached a third time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us what the people did with their mouths during the slaughtering: they said הלל the whole time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הלל was said for as long as the slaughtering lasted, so it was repeated if the work was not finished. The משנה adds that the כהנים worked so quickly that the third round never happened.

keyTerms.meaning: The praise chapters of תהלים (113–118)
They repeated it a second time
They did it a third time
Ever, in all their days

phrases.english: They read the Hallel.
If they finished, they repeated it,
and if they repeated it, they said it a third time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁלְּשׁוּ מִימֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: even though they never in their days said it a third time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds what was said during the slaughtering of each group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל is said throughout the slaughtering and repeated as needed, though a third time never happened.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the third group never reached אהבתי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the third group was so small that they finished before even reaching the chapter of אהבתי כי ישמע ה׳ in their first round of הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: The third group never even reached 'I love that ה׳ hears,' because it had so few people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a detail about the third group: it was so small that it never got far into הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two groups were big, but by the time the third group came in, few people were left. Their slaughtering ended before the people even reached the fourth chapter of הלל. This was the source of the nickname כת עצלנית (the lazy group), which the גמרא mentions later.

keyTerms.meaning: Opening of תהלים 116, a chapter in the middle of הלל
Few in number

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Never in the days of the third group

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִגִּיעוּ לְ״אָהַבְתִּי כִּי יִשְׁמַע ה׳״,
phrases.english: did they reach 'I love that the Lord hears,'
because its people were few.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: מִימֵיהֶם שֶׁל כַּת שְׁלִישִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the הלל description, specifically about the third group.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third group was so small it finished before reaching אהבתי.

steps.title: On שבת it is the same, but the floor is washed
steps.stepSummary: The קרבן פסח was done the same way on שבת as on a weekday. The one difference is that the כהנים washed the blood off the floor of the עזרה, and the חכמים did not approve of this.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is done on a weekday, so it is done on שבת. The only difference is that the כהנים rinse the courtyard floor, against the wishes of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now teaches what changes, and what does not, when ערב פסח falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח pushes aside שבת, so the whole procedure stays the same. The one difference is that the כהנים washed the floor, which is not needed for the קרבן itself, and the משנה notes that the חכמים were not happy about it. The גמרא will later discuss exactly what this means.

keyTerms.meaning: A weekday
Rinse, wash with water
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Without the approval of the Sages

phrases.english: As its procedure on a weekday,
so is its procedure on Shabbat,
except that the priests rinse the courtyard
not according to the will of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the general procedure to the special case of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The procedure is identical on שבת, except that the כהנים washed the עזרה floor without the חכמים' approval.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the קרבן פסח overrides שבת fully, while extra activities not needed for the קרבן are viewed differently.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a cup of the mixed blood was thrown on the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a כהן filled a cup from the mixed blood on the floor and threw it once on the מזבח. The חכמים disagreed with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He would fill a cup from the mixed blood and throw it once on top of the altar. The חכמים did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a step that was done with the blood on the floor before it was washed away, and the חכמים reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from many animals spilled and mixed on the floor. רבי יהודה holds that a cup of it was thrown on the מזבח, so that if any animal's blood spilled before it was thrown, its קרבן would still be valid. The חכמים disagree, so this is a מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixed blood (blood of many animals mixed together on the floor)
A cup
They did not agree with him

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He would fill a cup from the mixed blood,

phrases.aramaic: זְרָקוֹ זְרִיקָה אַחַת עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ.
phrases.english: and throw it with one throw upon the altar.
And the Sages did not agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כּוֹס הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִדַּם הַתַּעֲרוֹבֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי יהודה's view about the floor blood mentioned in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה says a cup of mixed blood was thrown on the מזבח, and the חכמים disagree.

steps.title: How the animals were hung and skinned
steps.stepSummary: Iron hooks in the walls and pillars were used to hang the animals for skinning. Anyone without room at a hook used a thin, smooth pole resting on his shoulder and a friend's shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did they hang and skin the animals? Iron hooks were fixed in the walls and pillars, and on them they hung and skinned. Anyone who had no spot used thin, smooth poles that were there. He put one on his shoulder and his friend's shoulder, and hung and skinned the animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the blood to the next job: hanging the animal and removing its skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks 'how' and then gives the practical setup. Fixed hooks were the normal method. Because there were so many people, there was a backup: two people held a pole between their shoulders as a portable hook.

keyTerms.meaning: They hang (the animal)
They skin (the animal)
Hooks
Poles, rods

phrases.english: How do they hang and skin?
Hooks of iron
were fixed in the walls and in the pillars,
on which they hang and skin.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לִתְלוֹת וּלְהַפְשִׁיט —
phrases.english: Anyone who has no place to hang and skin:
thin and smooth poles were there;

phrases.aramaic: מַנִּיחַ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְעַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵירוֹ,
phrases.english: he places one on his shoulder and on his fellow's shoulder,
and hangs and skins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the blood service to preparing the animal's body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals were hung on fixed iron hooks for skinning, or on poles held between two people's shoulders.
steps.confusionAlert: The question 'כיצד' here is the משנה's own way of opening a description. It is not a challenge.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר begins a view about the fourteenth on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts quoting רבי אליעזר about a case when the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת. His full statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: When the fourteenth...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה is opening רבי אליעזר's opinion, and the rest of it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Right after describing the poles, the משנה brings רבי אליעזר, who addresses when the fourteenth of ניסן falls on שבת, apparently about how the skinning is done then. The details come on the next amud, so for now just note that a new opinion is starting.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourteenth (of ניסן), the day the פסח is slaughtered

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: When the fourteenth

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces רבי אליעזר's view connected to the hanging and skinning in step 25. It continues on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of רבי אליעזר's statement about the fourteenth of ניסן. The ruling itself continues on the next amud.
